section_completion_log.section_name: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

revision_actions.description: Add an explicit gender-dimension paragraph to section 1.2 of the Excellence section. Either (a) identify how the gender dimension is incorporated into the research design — for example, diversity considerations in the farmer-engagement sample via AgroVIR, or representativeness considerations in ground-truth site selection in WP3 — or (b) explicitly state that the gender dimension is not applicable to this particular technical research domain and provide a one-paragraph justification. Either treatment satisfies the mandatory Excellence sub-criterion; its complete absence does not and will be flagged by evaluators.

Add a concise publication and research-output summary to section 1.4 of the Excellence section, listing key peer-reviewed publications by Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (journal name, year, brief contribution statement), any conference papers, open datasets, or open software contributions, and any evidence of peer recognition such as journal reviewing, competitive grants, or invited presentations. This evidence is essential for evaluators assessing the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills sub-criterion; its absence is a material gap for a competitive MSCA-PF application.
revision_actions.reason: Section 1.4 refers qualitatively to Dr. Cholakova's peer-reviewed work on maize chilling-stress photosynthesis and biostimulants but provides no enumerated publication list (journal names, years, contribution statements), no conference or open-dataset record, and no peer-recognition evidence; resolving requires specific bibliographic data absent from the confirmed Tier 3 sources within the declared input set (§13.3 — missing publication record and peer-recognition data for the fellow).

revision_actions.description: In section 1.2 of the Excellence section, specify the primary model family for WP1 Task T1-03 as the Bayesian hierarchical model, with a brief methodological justification (e.g., hierarchical structure matches the multi-level field/crop/sensor data architecture), and frame the Gaussian process as an explicitly documented fallback alternative if the hierarchical model proves computationally intractable at project scale. Remove the 'model family decided at MS2 review' framing that presents the core modelling choice as unresolved at proposal stage.
revision_actions.reason: Section 1.2 still describes Route A candidate families as 'Bayesian hierarchical model, Gaussian process, or probabilistic machine learning more broadly' without specifying BHM as primary for T1-03; implementation section 3.1 retains the 'model family decided at MS2 review' framing; no new prose in section 1.2 commits to BHM as the primary choice — resolving requires new prose in section 1.2 of the excellence section, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle.

revision_actions.description: Add indicative minimum quantitative targets to section 1.3 of the Excellence section for the training programme: for example, at least two peer-reviewed journal submissions during the fellowship; a minimum of N structured training hours per MSCA mandatory dimension; at least one conference presentation per project year; at least one documented knowledge-exchange event per year at ELTE. State explicitly that these indicative floors will be confirmed and refined in D4-01 with the supervisor, preserving the principled deferral while giving evaluators a credibility anchor for the training sub-criterion.
revision_actions.reason: Section 1.3 explicitly characterises the absence of quantitative targets as a deliberate design decision, deferring all specific figures (publication counts, training hours, conference presentations) to D4-01; no indicative minimums have been added to section 1.3 — resolving requires new prose in sub-section 1.3, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle on that sub-section.

revision_actions.description: In section 2.2 of the Impact section, name specific target venues for scientific dissemination: at minimum two to three relevant conference series (e.g., IEEE IGARSS, ISPRS Congress, ECPA European Conference on Precision Agriculture) and two to three target journal families (e.g., Remote Sensing of Environment, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture) aligned with the project's OUT-1, OUT-2, and OUT-3 outputs. Also identify the preprint repository to be used for Plan S compliance. This specificity allows evaluators to assess the suitability of the dissemination measures against the target scientific communities.
revision_actions.reason: Section 2.2 states that conference activities are planned at 'at least one presentation per project year' but names no specific conference series, journal families, or preprint repository; the dissemination plan remains generic as to venue — resolving requires new prose naming specific venues in sub-section 2.2, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle.

revision_actions.description: In section 2.3 of the Impact section, add two to three published background statistics contextualising the scale of the irrigation efficiency challenge in the target region or sector — for example, EUROSTAT irrigated area data for Hungarian horticulture, FAO water-use benchmarks for tomato, or agronomic literature estimates of yield losses attributable to late stress detection. These data ground the IMP-2 magnitude claim without asserting project-level economic outcomes that a TRL 3-4 research fellowship cannot warrant. Cite sources explicitly so evaluators can verify the contextual scale claims.
revision_actions.reason: Section 2.3 explicitly states 'No specific water-saving percentages, yield improvement figures, or economic return estimates are asserted in any Tier 1–4 source for this project, and no such figures are invented here' and provides no published background statistics contextualising the irrigation efficiency challenge scale; resolving requires adding cited external reference data (EUROSTAT, FAO, agronomic literature) not present in the declared Tier 3 inputs and new prose in sub-section 2.3, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle.

revision_actions.description: In section 2.1 of the Impact section, either describe any structured technology-transfer or co-design activities with AgroVIR that go beyond field access (e.g., documented user-requirements workshops or feedback-loop sessions with a formal time commitment) and explicitly frame them as inter-sectoral training activities; or directly acknowledge the absence of a formal secondment and make a stronger evidence-based argument for why AgroVIR's operational feedback loop and Dr. Jung's co-founder mentoring together constitute credible inter-sectoral career development for the stated MSCA-PF employability objectives.
revision_actions.reason: Section 2.1 briefly references AgroVIR's applied-sector dimension in the context of knowledge valorisation training and mentions Dr. Jung's entrepreneurial mentoring, but does not describe any structured inter-sectoral activities with AgroVIR carrying formal time commitments and does not make a substantially strengthened standalone argument for inter-sectoral career development adequacy — resolving requires new prose in sub-section 2.1, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle.

revision_actions.description: In section 3.1.4 (T3-03 task description) or section 3.1.6 (risk assessment), add explicit mitigation for the two-month T3-03 window: document that preparatory statistical scripting and analysis-protocol setup for the RQ5 and RQ9 assessments will be completed within T3-02 (months 18-20) so that quantitative analysis can begin before data collection formally closes at month 20, or specify a contingency analysis plan for partial-season data if full seasonal collection is delayed by weather or access constraints.
revision_actions.reason: The T3-03 task description and section 3.1.6 risk register address data-access, validation, model-complexity, and operationalisation risks but include no explicit mitigation for the tight two-month T3-03 window, no mention of preparatory statistical scripting within T3-02 months 18-20, and no partial-season contingency analysis plan — resolving requires new prose in section 3.1, deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle on sub-section 3.1.

revision_actions.description: In section 3.2.2 of the Implementation section, add a factual statement confirming whether Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) holds an active, published gender equality plan (with a reference URL if publicly available) and whether ELTE holds the European Charter for Researchers HRS4R label. If ELTE holds the HRS4R label, cite it explicitly: this citation satisfies the hosting arrangements sub-criterion in the evaluation form without further justification per the form's explicit text.
revision_actions.reason: Section 3.2.2 states that ELTE is 'subject to the Horizon Europe requirement to hold and maintain a gender equality plan at grant signature and during the grant period' but does not confirm whether ELTE actually holds an active published GEP, provides no URL, and makes no mention of the HRS4R label; resolving requires factual institutional compliance data (GEP URL, HRS4R status) absent from Tier 3 sources within the declared input set (§13.3 — missing institutional compliance data), deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle on sub-section 3.2.2.

revision_actions.description: In section 3.2.2 of the Implementation section, add a short paragraph summarising ELTE's broader institutional research profile relevant to the fellowship: Horizon Europe or FP9 grant history in geoinformatics or agri-EO contexts, ERA network or consortium memberships, relevant international research partnerships, and ELTE's institutional open-access and FAIR data policy. This provides evaluators with institution-level evidence for the 'quality and capacity of the host institution' sub-criterion that is independent of the individual supervisor's credentials.
revision_actions.reason: Section 3.2.2 addresses ELTE's hosting capacity exclusively at the group and supervisor level (Multisensor-Drone-Fusion Working Group, Dr. Jung's dual habilitations and co-founderships) with no institution-level research profile data (Horizon Europe grant history, ERA memberships, international partnerships, institutional FAIR data policy); resolving requires factual institutional profile data absent from Tier 3 sources within the declared input set (§13.3 — missing institution-level research capacity data), deferred to an operator-directed revision cycle on sub-section 3.2.2.
